args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate 18% in all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.1 was also unhealthy as v2.3.1-rc in staging. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback finished and was verified in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Next steps: confirm health checks and error rate have recovered, and find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with health checks failing and an 18% error rate. The test build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0.
- **Check afterward:** I checked the service again after the rollback. It reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says what failed, that I rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and what to do next: keep watching the service and find what's wrong in v2.3.1 before deploying it again. I wrote the summary before the post-rollback check came back, so it says the rollback was verified but doesn't include the recovered health numbers.

No approval was needed: the change-manager rule only applies to versions that have never been healthy in production, and v2.3.0 has been.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
